producer_report.summary: The decisions page now lists only proposals that are open and above the raising role's limit. With none it shows one line, 'Nothing waiting for you'. The cause of the within-limit listing is certain; the cause of the stale decided proposals is not proven. `render()` listed everything `read_snapshot` returned, and `read_snapshot` removed only proposals named by a work decision. No code applied the role limit, so a proposal the role may change itself (such as ne91) was shown. I added `is_owners_to_decide` in xtask/src/decisions.rs, which `render()` now applies. The rule is the same as `in_limit` in athena-core and uses the shared `may_change`. A role with no recorded definition counts as above the limit. xtask does not depend on athena-core, so the rule is written again, and a code comment says why. Approved and rejected proposals were already dropped at base: approve-work and reject-work commit to the current branch (main) through `commit_records`, and `read_snapshot` already reads main's tree and the records branch. I could not reproduce a decided proposal showing through `locate()`. The likely cause is a stale page, because pages.yml runs only on a push to main. That workflow is out of scope; the changelog and this report name it and propose a schedule trigger. In the evidence snapshot, decisions for qyd9, jtd2 and ne91 are all on main.

open_issues: The reason a decided proposal showed on the live page on 3 Nov is not proven. The base code already read main's decisions. The likely cause is that pages.yml rebuilds only on a push to main, so a scheduled or records-branch-triggered rebuild would fix it. That workflow is out of scope and I did not edit it.
The read of main's decisions swallows listing errors with unwrap_or_default(). I left that as it was.
mistakes: My first call to the Bash tool used `tail`, which is not allowed; I reran without it.
I wrote a stray `old_str` parameter in one Edit call. The edit still applied correctly, and the final file has the intended text.
learnings: approve-work and reject-work commit through commit_records onto the current branch (main), not the records branch. The decisions page reads main's tree (HEAD) for that reason.

In athena_data, may_change(limit, rung) is true when rung >= HIGHEST_SELF_CHANGE and rung >= limit. Enum order puts OwnerGoals lowest and Implementation highest, so a design-decisions proposal is above a defaults-conventions limit.
pages.yml triggers only on a push to main or manual dispatch, so a decision or proposal written later does not rebuild decisions.html until the next push.
desires: A way to rerun the new tests against the base source automatically; I disabled the filter by hand to show the failures.
